hypothesis: The batched-judging-helps camp and the comparison-hurts camp are both right because they measure on different pool states: on real competition math, simultaneous pooling raises recall of a present correct answer (pools of 2 to 3) but makes the judge pick a wrong answer from target-absent pools at a flat rate of roughly 0.5 or more, far above what independent isolated verdicts predict, and this holds for sonnet as well as haiku.
gap_with_citations: Helps: BatchEval arXiv 2401.00437 (+10.5% Pearson at 64% cost); batched self-consistency arXiv 2505.12570 (NDCG@10 43.8 to 51.3); Zhao et al. arXiv 2502.01839 (comparing across responses locates errors, larger pools improve self-verification); arXiv 2606.09409 (pairwise Elo Spearman above 0.9). Hurts: Jeong et al. arXiv 2406.12319 'Comparative Trap'; arXiv 2504.14716 (pairwise flips about 35% vs 9% absolute); arXiv 2606.13685 (judges pick a pairwise winner when pointwise scores show no difference). Opposite direction: Han et al. arXiv 2608.23941 (longer review unit makes verifier more rejective). The atlas gap C-G3/X-G7 notes no paper on either side conditions on target presence. The in-house frontier run (corpus/02-lineup-problem-verifier/frontier-run/paper.md) found the reconciliation only on 72 synthetic arithmetic items, haiku only; its own limitations section asks for real tasks and a frontier judge, with the choosing rate as the registered primary. Verification status: all ids taken from corpus (atlas papers_all.json and novelty audit C, fetch-verified by those sweeps); none re-verified this session because arxiv.org is not reachable from this VM.
prediction: On target-absent pools of MATH level 4-5 wrong answers, per-pool any-accept rate at n=4 is >= 0.45 for haiku and >= 0.35 for sonnet, versus <= 0.25 predicted by independence from each candidate's isolated (serial) accept rate. On target-present pools, recall of gold at n=2 exceeds isolated recall by >= 0.05.
kill_criterion: Kill the reconciliation if, for haiku, the observed target-absent any-accept rate at n=4 minus the independence-predicted rate has a 95% item-bootstrap CI upper bound below +0.10, OR if target-present recall at n=2 is not higher than isolated recall (difference CI lower bound <= 0 and point estimate <= 0). Kill the 'holds for sonnet' clause if the sonnet excess is below +0.05 (CI upper bound).
smallest_experiment: Items: 80 MATH level 4-5 test problems from github.com/openai/prm800k (math_splits/test.jsonl) with sympy-equivalence grading; candidate wrong answers are genuine haiku/sonnet errors from 6 prompt-varied solver samples per item (keep items with >= 4 distinct wrong final answers). Arms: isolated-serial (each candidate judged alone, 4 verdicts per prompt in serial format), simultaneous pool n=2 and n=4, each target-absent and target-present (gold + wrongs), 2 slot orders. Models: haiku judge (all arms), sonnet judge (n=4 absent/present and serial only). Calls: generation 480 haiku + 80 sonnet; judging haiku 80 items x (1 serial + 4 pool cells) x 2 orders = 800; sonnet 80 x 3 x 1 = 240. Total about 1,280 haiku, 320 sonnet.
why_it_matters: Every best-of-n, tournament and co-scientist ranker assumes a constant verifier false-accept rate and is validated on target-present material. If the choosing rate is a pool property on real math and survives a stronger judge, pooled verification is unsafe exactly in the hard, low-coverage regime, and serial verdicts are a free fix.
scoop_risk: Medium. The eyewitness bridge is unclaimed per audit C, but 2608.17270 could add a target-absent arm in v2 and 2608.23941 / 2608.16003 are working the same SDT criterion question.

hypothesis: Debate helps a weak judge only when the debaters hold information the judge lacks; on the same code-correctness items, giving the debaters (sonnet) unit-test execution traces that the judge (haiku) cannot see produces a debate-over-direct-judging gain, while the identical protocol without the asymmetry produces none.
gap_with_citations: Debate helps: Khan et al. arXiv 2402.06782 'Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers' (non-expert LLM judges 76% vs 48% naive on QuALITY, an information-asymmetric reading task) [VERIFIED this session via web search]. Mixed: Kenton et al. arXiv 2407.04622 'On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs' (NeurIPS 2024): debate beats direct QA in extractive tasks with information asymmetry, but results are mixed on tasks without it, with small or no advantage over QA when the judge is weaker [VERIFIED this session via web search]. Conditional: Elasky, Nakasako, Goyal arXiv 2605.27483 'Debate Helps Weak Judges Reward Stronger Models' (code and logic; gains only when the critic out-classifies the judge and the judge checks claims; significant in 3 of 5 pairings) [VERIFIED this session via web search]. Also corpus: 'Debate or Vote' arXiv 2508.17536 (debate as martingale, no added information); arXiv 2609.35875 (debate ties or loses to matched-budget voting). No paper manipulates information asymmetry as a factor within one item set with programmatic gold.
prediction: With asymmetry (debaters see test traces): debate accuracy minus direct-judge accuracy >= +0.10. Without asymmetry: difference within [-0.03, +0.03]. Interaction (asym gain minus no-asym gain) >= +0.08.
kill_criterion: Kill if the asymmetry x protocol interaction has a 95% item-bootstrap CI that includes 0, or if the no-asymmetry debate gain is >= the asymmetry debate gain. Secondary kill: if debate without asymmetry beats direct by >= +0.08 (CI excludes 0), the information-asymmetry account is wrong.
smallest_experiment: Items: 100 (problem, candidate solution) pairs from MBPP (github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/mbpp) and HumanEval (github.com/openai/human-eval), half passing and half failing the hidden tests, candidates generated by haiku. Gold: test execution. Arms (2x2 plus consultancy): {asymmetry: debaters get the pytest output, none} x {direct haiku judge, one-round sonnet debate (pro vs con, one rebuttal), sonnet consultancy random side}. Judge always haiku, never sees test output. Calls: debaters 100 items x 2 asym levels x 2 sides x 2 turns = 800 sonnet would exceed budget, so use 1 turn each (no rebuttal, which 2605.27483 found not to matter): 400 sonnet debater calls + 200 consultancy = 600 sonnet; reduce to 60 items -> 360 sonnet; haiku judges 60 x 2 x 3 arms x 3 repeats = 1,080 haiku.
why_it_matters: Scalable-oversight agendas rest on debate helping weak judges. If the gain is entirely an information-transfer channel, debate offers nothing beyond giving the judge the evidence directly, and the protocol should be redesigned around evidence surfacing rather than adversarial argument.
scoop_risk: Medium. 2605.27483 is close (code/logic, critic-classification condition) but does not manipulate asymmetry within items; a follow-up from that group or DeepMind could.

hypothesis: Whether peer argument content matters (versus only the displayed answer) is decided by whether the receiver can check the argument: on items the receiver solves reliably alone, a valid argument for the wrong label is rejected and an invalid argument for the correct label is discounted (content dominates); on items it cannot solve, the displayed answer drives revision regardless of argument validity (label dominates).
gap_with_citations: Label camp: Shu arXiv 2609.26145 'Unanimity Without Persuasion' (labels without reasoning reproduce 91.5% of collapse; full debate adds 4.3 points); Ringelmann arXiv 2606.02646 (noise placebo tracks debate gains); arXiv 2607.05545 (speaker-free harmful revision floor 66.5%). Content camp: Kumarappan arXiv 2605.12991 'Not Just RLHF' (one correctly arguing dissenter cuts susceptibility 54 to 73 pp); arXiv 2608.07920 (matched-content label swap null, quote content drives anchoring); Elasky arXiv 2605.27483 [VERIFIED this session]. Atlas gap B-G1: nobody has crossed content validity with answer display. Audit B: 'checker-graded valid/invalid critiques' is the unclaimed piece. Ids other than 2605.27483 taken from corpus (novelty audit B, fetch-verified there), not re-verified this session.
prediction: Define content effect = P(adopt peer answer | valid argument) - P(adopt | invalid argument), with displayed answer held fixed. On receiver-solvable items (5/5 isolated correct) content effect >= 0.25; on receiver-unsolvable items (0-2/5) content effect <= 0.10. Interaction >= 0.15.
kill_criterion: Kill if the solvability x validity interaction 95% CI includes 0, or if content effect on unsolvable items is >= content effect on solvable items. Also kill the label-dominance half if on unsolvable items the displayed-answer effect (wrong vs correct label, invalid argument both) is < 0.15.
smallest_experiment: Items: 120 GSM8K test problems (github.com/openai/grade-school-math) plus 120 MATH level 3-5 (prm800k) so haiku solvability spans 0/5 to 5/5. Pre-step: 5 isolated haiku solves per item (1,200 calls) to stratify. Peer messages built programmatically: valid argument = gold solution steps; invalid argument = gold steps with one verifiable arithmetic step altered (checker confirms the step is wrong). 2x2 crossing: displayed answer {gold, wrong} x argument {valid-for-displayed-answer, invalid}; for wrong label + valid content use a correct derivation that ends with a transcription slip to the wrong answer. Receiver: haiku gives initial answer then sees the peer message, 1 call per cell per item: 240 x 4 = 960 haiku. Sonnet replication on 60 unsolvable-for-haiku items: 240 sonnet. Total about 2,160 haiku, 240 sonnet.
why_it_matters: If content matters only when checkable, debate and critique are useful exactly where they are least needed, and oversight on hard items reduces to conformity to labels. That is a direct statement about when MAS communication carries information.
scoop_risk: Medium-high. Many 2026 conformity papers (audit B: B2 'heavily partially preempted'); the solvability-stratified 2x2 with checker-graded validity is the narrow unclaimed piece.

hypothesis: The disagreement over whether prompt-level diversity decorrelates same-model agents is an artefact of unmatched member accuracy: once haiku instances are matched on solo accuracy, strategy-level diversification (different solution methods) lowers the same-wrong-answer rate relative to temperature-like resampling, while persona diversification does not.
gap_with_citations: Diversity useless or harmful: arXiv 2609.35875 'Beyond Symmetric Agents' (persona prompting a 'persona tax', 23 models); Nitarach arXiv 2603.27844 (every prompt-level diversification failed in AIMO 3); Ringelmann arXiv 2606.02646 (only architectural diversity lowers the correlation constant). Diversity helps: ICLR 2027 submission OpenReview A8fKFiZMnu 'One Model, Many Minds' (strategy diversification lowers rho 0.69 to 0.60; rephrasing does not); OpenReview Co5FYGRDkp (persona helps in mixed-model groups). Confound: arXiv 2607.20768 (diversity metrics nearly collinear with 1 minus mean accuracy, rho 0.99). Also Kim et al. arXiv 2506.07962 (models agree on the same wrong answer). Audit A8 flags this as 'contested'. All from corpus; none re-verified this session; OpenReview ids could not be re-checked (bot challenge per audit summary).
prediction: On items where at least two arms err, pairwise P(same wrong answer | both wrong) is >= 0.08 lower for strategy-diverse pairs than for plain-resample pairs at matched accuracy (|acc diff| <= 0.03); persona-diverse pairs differ from plain-resample by < 0.03. Majority-of-5 accuracy is higher for strategy-diverse than plain by >= 0.03.
kill_criterion: Kill if the strategy minus plain difference in same-wrong-answer rate has 95% item-bootstrap CI upper bound above -0.02 (i.e., no reliable decorrelation), or if matching accuracy is impossible (arm accuracies differ by > 0.05 after reweighting) in which case report as inconclusive, not support.
smallest_experiment: Items: 200 MATH level 4-5 problems with numeric/sympy-checkable answers (prm800k test split), where haiku accuracy is about 40 to 70%. Arms (haiku only, 5 samples per item per arm): plain (same prompt, 5 independent calls), persona (5 personas: statistician, engineer, etc.), strategy (5 methods: direct algebra, casework, work backwards, small-case pattern then prove, estimate-then-verify). Calls: 200 x 3 x 5 = 3,000 haiku. Accuracy matching by item-level reweighting or by dropping the strategy prompts whose solo accuracy deviates > 0.03. Optional 50-item sonnet plain arm (250 calls) as the architectural-diversity reference.
why_it_matters: MAS designers spend tokens on persona panels. If only method diversity buys independence once accuracy is controlled, persona panels are a pure tax and the Ringelmann/K* effective-n laws need a method-diversity term.
scoop_risk: High. A8fKFiZMnu already reports the strategy result; novelty is the accuracy-matched three-way adjudication on Claude models, i.e. a replication-with-control.

hypothesis: Same-model verification looks helpful in test-time-scaling papers and harmful in self-review papers because the harm comes from shared errors, not self-recognition: haiku accepts its own wrong answers more than sonnet's wrong answers, but the gap disappears when the comparison is restricted to wrong answers that haiku itself would independently produce.
gap_with_citations: Pays: Multi-Agent Verification arXiv 2502.20379 (self-improvement works with the same base model verifying); Zhao et al. arXiv 2502.01839 (scaling self-verification pays). Fails: ICLR 2027 submission OpenReview MN8GotJuVL 'Two Asymmetries of LLM Self-Review' (self-review FPR 16.0% vs 0.0% cross-review at matched recall); arXiv 2609.04270 (same-model self-review falsely rejects 35% of correct answers vs 2% cross-family); arXiv 2605.10850 'verification mirage' (verifier error more likely when generator wrong); Dastidar arXiv 2607.17044. Atlas gap X-G9 states the contradiction. From corpus (audit A and atlas X), not re-verified this session.
prediction: Raw: haiku false-accept rate on haiku-generated wrong answers exceeds that on sonnet-generated wrong answers by >= 0.08. Stratified: within wrong answers that match an answer string haiku produced in its own independent samples on that item, own-vs-other provenance changes false-accept by < 0.03; a provenance label ('you wrote this' vs 'another model wrote this') on identical text changes it by < 0.03.
kill_criterion: Kill the shared-error account if, after restricting to wrong answers present in haiku's own sample set, the own-minus-other false-accept difference remains >= 0.06 with CI excluding 0, or if the provenance label alone shifts false-accept by >= 0.06 (that would indicate self-recognition/self-preference).
smallest_experiment: Items: 150 MATH level 3-5 problems (prm800k). Generation: 6 haiku and 3 sonnet samples per item (900 haiku, 450 sonnet; cut sonnet to 100 items x 2 = 200 if over budget). Verification: haiku judges each distinct wrong answer and a gold answer in isolation, 2 provenance-label conditions on a 50% subsample. Approx 150 items x ~4 distinct candidates x 1.5 = 900 haiku verification calls. Total about 1,800 haiku, 200 to 300 sonnet.
why_it_matters: Co-scientist pipelines use one model family for generation, review and ranking. If the harm is shared error rather than self-identity, anonymizing provenance fixes nothing and only cross-family or tool-grounded verifiers add evidence.
scoop_risk: Medium. MN8GotJuVL and 2609.04270 measure the gap; decomposing it into shared error vs self-recognition with the label manipulation was not found in the corpus.

hypothesis: Authority and identity labels move LLM answers only under item-level uncertainty: an 'expert' label attached to a wrong answer flips haiku on items it is unsure about but not on items it solves consistently, which reconciles reports that labels drive conformity with a matched-content label-swap null and with reports that competence signals help.
gap_with_citations: Labels matter: 'Who Do LLMs Trust?' arXiv 2602.13568 (conform to 'human expert' labels even when wrong); Choi et al. arXiv 2510.07517 'When Identity Skews Debate' (ACL 2026; sycophancy dominates; anonymization reduces bias); arXiv 2606.01637 (authority labels raise endorsement regardless of correctness). Labels null or helpful: arXiv 2608.07920 (self vs peer matched-content swap, -0.17 pp, CI -0.68 to 0.35); arXiv 2607.05545 (minimal person labels do not raise the floor); arXiv 2601.21742 and 2604.02668 (accurate reliability signals help). Atlas gap B-G3: the literature never conditions on whether the receiver could solve the item. Audit B4: the difficulty x competence-gap crossover is untested. From corpus; not re-verified this session.
prediction: Expert-label effect = P(switch to wrong labelled answer | expert label) - P(switch | anonymous). On high-consistency items (5/5 isolated correct): <= 0.05. On low-consistency items (1-3/5): >= 0.20. Symmetric: an expert label on the correct answer raises adoption on low-consistency items by >= 0.15 and on high-consistency items by <= 0.05.
kill_criterion: Kill if the consistency-stratum x label interaction 95% CI includes 0, or if the expert-label effect on high-consistency items is >= 0.10 (labels override knowledge, the uncertainty-gating account fails).
smallest_experiment: Items: reuse K3's 240 GSM8K+MATH items with 5-sample haiku consistency strata (shared 1,200 pre-calls; if run standalone, 1,200 haiku). Arms: peer message gives an answer only (no argument) with source label {anonymous agent, 'a peer model', 'a domain expert (PhD mathematician)', 'a weaker model'} x displayed answer {gold, most common wrong}. 240 x 4 x 2 = 1,920 haiku. Sonnet on 60 items, 2 labels x 2 answers = 240 sonnet.
why_it_matters: Debate and MAS frameworks either anonymize agents (2510.07517) or broadcast reputation (2601.21742). If label power is uncertainty-gated, the right policy is conditional: show competence signals only where the receiver is uncertain, and anonymize elsewhere.
scoop_risk: Medium. Several conformity groups are active (Hu and Qu series); the explicit consistency-stratified crossover was flagged unclaimed in audit B4.

hypothesis: Pairwise comparison beats direct scoring at ranking candidates by correctness only because most pairs differ in correctness; on pairs where both code solutions fail the tests, haiku's pairwise winner is no better than chance at picking the solution that passes more tests, while pointwise test-pass estimates retain signal.
gap_with_citations: Pairwise helps: 'Correct Looks Better' arXiv 2606.09409 (Elo Spearman above 0.9 with accuracy; pairwise substantially beats direct evaluation for weak judges; notes most judgments fall on both-correct or both-wrong pairs); arXiv 2607.15766 (arena evaluation resolves finer differences than rubric scoring); arXiv 2507.17797 GenSelect. Pairwise hurts: Rajwal et al. arXiv 2608.17270 (intrinsic non-comparative scoring Hit@1 33.0% beats prompted listwise 16.6%); arXiv 2606.12071 (novelty mirage stronger in comparative evaluation); arXiv 2504.14716 (pairwise flips 35% vs 9%); arXiv 2606.13685. Atlas gaps C-G4 and X-G7. From corpus; not re-verified this session.
prediction: On mixed pairs (one passes all tests, one fails) pairwise picks the passing solution >= 0.80 and beats pointwise-score comparison by >= 0.05. On both-fail pairs with test-pass fractions differing by >= 0.3, pairwise agreement with the higher-pass solution is <= 0.58, and pointwise predicted-pass-fraction comparison is >= pairwise + 0.05.
kill_criterion: Kill if on both-fail pairs pairwise agreement with the higher-pass-fraction solution has 95% CI lower bound >= 0.62 (pairwise retains signal where predicted not to), or if pointwise does not beat pairwise there (difference CI includes 0 and point estimate <= 0).
smallest_experiment: Items: 120 MBPP/HumanEval problems with extended tests (EvalPlus tests via github.com/evalplus/evalplus release files if git-cloneable, else original tests plus 10 generated property tests checked against the reference solution). Candidates: 6 haiku solutions per item, test-pass fraction computed by execution (CPU sandbox). Pairs: 3 mixed + 3 both-fail per item where available (target about 300 each). Arms: pairwise haiku judge (2 orders) vs pointwise haiku 'estimate fraction of tests passed' on each candidate. Calls: generation 720 haiku; pairwise 600 x 2 = 1,200 haiku; pointwise 720 haiku. Sonnet pairwise on 100 both-fail pairs: 200 sonnet.
why_it_matters: AI-scientist evaluation is moving to arenas and Elo on the strength of correlation with accuracy. If pairwise signal vanishes when neither candidate is right, arena rankings in discovery settings (where most hypotheses are wrong) are uninformative at the top.
scoop_risk: Low-medium. 2606.09409 observed the both-wrong concentration but did not test signal within it; no code-execution graded version found in the corpus.

hypothesis: Whether sequential refinement or parallel sampling wins at matched compute is predicted by two measurable per-model, per-difficulty transition rates (P(wrong->right) and P(right->wrong) under one revision step) and the parallel coverage curve; the sign flips between haiku and sonnet and between difficulty bands exactly where these rates predict.
gap_with_citations: Sequential wins: 'The Sequential Edge' arXiv 2511.02309 (95.6% of configurations). Parallel wins: arXiv 2604.05868 (parallel beats sequential in large reasoning models, attributed to lack of exploration); arXiv 2605.08478 (independent sampling wins per dollar on Codeforces). Difficulty moderation contested: Snell et al. arXiv 2408.03314 (easy items favour sequential revision) vs ICLR 2027 submission OpenReview NObhgEl9bp (depth wins on harder groups); arXiv 2604.22273 (self-correction degrades 4 of 7 models, ECR/EIR threshold). Atlas gap A-G2. From corpus; not re-verified this session.
prediction: A two-state Markov model fitted on a 40% calibration split (transition rates per model x difficulty band) plus the parallel majority-vote curve predicts the winner (sequential vs parallel at 4 matched calls) correctly in >= 5 of 6 held-out model x difficulty cells, and the predicted accuracy gap is within 0.06 of observed in >= 4 of 6.
kill_criterion: Kill if the model predicts the wrong sign in >= 2 of 6 held-out cells where the observed gap's CI excludes 0, or if the observed winner does not differ across any cell (no contradiction to explain on this substrate; report as null).
smallest_experiment: Items: 300 MATH problems, 100 each from levels 1-2, 3, 5 (prm800k test). Models: haiku (all 300), sonnet (90, 30 per band). Arms at matched 4 calls: parallel (4 independent solves, majority vote) vs sequential (solve, then 3 self-revision calls seeing the previous attempt). Calls: haiku 300 x 8 = 2,400; sonnet 90 x 8 = 720 (cut to 60 items -> 480 sonnet). Transition rates are read off the sequential chains on the calibration split.
why_it_matters: Converts a sign dispute between named papers into a predictive law from cheaply measured rates, which tells MAS designers in advance whether to iterate or fan out for a given model and task.
scoop_risk: Medium. 2604.22273 gives the ECR/EIR threshold for single-agent iteration; pitting it against parallel coverage as an out-of-sample sign predictor across the named contradiction was not found.

hypothesis: Showing peer confidence in debate has little effect in some studies and helps in others because the effect depends on calibration: haiku's verbalized confidences are poorly calibrated, so displaying them adds nothing over shuffled confidences, while displaying calibrated confidence (empirical accuracy of that bin) improves final accuracy.
gap_with_citations: Limited effect: Wu et al. arXiv 2511.07784 'Can LLM Agents Really Debate?' (confidence visibility offers limited gains). Helps: Zhu et al. arXiv 2601.19921 'Demystifying Multi-Agent Debate: The Role of Confidence and Diversity' (confidence-modulated updates drift debate to the correct answer); ConfMAD arXiv 2509.14034 (EMNLP 2025 Findings; confidence expression improves debate, inappropriate confidence causes stubbornness). Audit B4 lists these as 'mixed results'. From corpus; not re-verified this session.
prediction: Final 3-agent, 2-round haiku debate accuracy: raw-verbalized-confidence arm minus shuffled-confidence arm within [-0.02, +0.02]; calibrated-confidence arm minus shuffled >= +0.04; calibrated arm reduces right-to-wrong flips by >= 25% relative.
kill_criterion: Kill if the calibrated-minus-shuffled accuracy difference has 95% item-bootstrap CI upper bound below +0.02, or if raw-minus-shuffled is >= +0.04 with CI excluding 0 (raw confidence already informative, calibration account unnecessary).
smallest_experiment: Items: 200 MATH level 3-5 (prm800k). Round 0: 3 haiku solves per item with verbalized confidence 0-100 (600 calls); calibration map fitted on a separate 100-item split (300 calls). Round 1-2 updates in 4 arms (no confidence, raw, shuffled across items, calibrated): 200 x 4 arms x 3 agents x 2 rounds = 4,800, so cut to 1 round: 2,400 haiku. Total about 3,300 haiku, no larger models required (optional 40-item sonnet raw-vs-calibrated check, 240 sonnet).
why_it_matters: Confidence-weighted debate and voting are standard proposals; if raw LLM confidence is noise in this role, those mechanisms need an external calibration step, which is cheap and testable.
scoop_risk: Medium. Confidence in debate is studied (three papers above); the shuffled-confidence placebo with a calibrated arm on Claude models was not found in the corpus.
